summaryBox.title: Arrhenius Equation
summaryBox.takeaway: k = A e^(-E_a / RT). TC = k_(T+10) / k_T ≈ 2 to 3. Rate doubles because the Boltzmann fraction e^(-E_a/RT) expands exponentially.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
TEMPERATURE COEFFICIENT (TC)
                           
   $$\mathbf{\text{TC} = \frac{k_{T + 10^\circ\text{C}}}{k_T} \approx 2 \text{ to } 3}$$
   For most chemical reactions, a $10^\circ\text{C}$ rise in temperature DOUBLES or TRIPLES the rate constant $k$.

6.1 The Arrhenius Equation (Svante Arrhenius, 1889)

   $$\mathbf{k = A e^{-E_a / RT}}$$

   • A = Frequency Factor / Pre-exponential Factor
   • E_a = Activation Energy (J/mol or kJ/mol)
   • R = 8.314 J/mol·K (Gas Constant)
   • e^(-E_a / RT) = Boltzmann Factor (fraction of molecules possessing energy ≥ E_a)
conceptBreakdown.content:
Reaction rates increase sharply with increasing temperature:
$$\mathbf{\text{TC} = \frac{k_{T + 10^\circ\text{C}}}{k_T} \approx 2 \text{ to } 3}$$

### 6.1 The Arrhenius Equation (Svante Arrhenius, 1889)
Quantifies the temperature dependence of the rate constant $k$:
$$\mathbf{k = A e^{-E_a / RT}}$$
where:
- $A$ = Frequency Factor / Pre-exponential Factor (measures total collision frequency and orientation)
- $E_a$ = Activation Energy ($\text{J/mol}$ or $\text{kJ/mol}$)
- $R = 8.314\text{ J/mol}\cdot\text{K}$ (Gas Constant)
- $e^{-E_a / RT}$ = Boltzmann Factor (fraction of molecules possessing energy $\ge E_a$)

conceptBreakdown.title: 6.2 Linear Arrhenius Plots & Two-Temperature Equation
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ARRHENIUS LINEAR PLOTS
                       
   Logarithmic Form:   $$\mathbf{\ln k = \ln A - \frac{E_a}{RT}} \implies \mathbf{\log_{10} k = \log_{10} A - \frac{E_a}{2.303 RT}}$$

                        ARRHENIUS GRAPHICAL PLOT
                        
       log₁₀ k ▲
               │ * (y-intercept = log₁₀ A)
               │  \
               │   \  Slope = -E_a / (2.303 R)
               │    \
             0 └─────*───────────► 1/T (K⁻¹)

6.2 Two-Temperature Form of Arrhenius Equation:
$$\mathbf{\log_{10} \left( \frac{k_2}{k_1} \right) = \frac{E_a}{2.303 R} \left( \frac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1 T_2} \right) = \frac{E_a}{2.303 R} \left( \frac{1}{T_1} - \frac{1}{T_2} \right)}$$
conceptBreakdown.content:
Evaluating rate constants $k_1$ and $k_2$ at temperatures $T_1$ and $T_2$ ($T_2 > T_1$):
$$\mathbf{\log_{10} \left( \frac{k_2}{k_1} \right) = \frac{E_a}{2.303 R} \left( \frac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1 T_2} \right) = \frac{E_a}{2.303 R} \left( \frac{1}{T_1} - \frac{1}{T_2} \right)}$$

quickRevision: Slope of ln k vs 1/T is -E_a / R.
Slope of log₁₀ k vs 1/T is -E_a / (2.303 R).
